content: Root cause: The bug was caused by a use-after-free issue in the handling of the per-cpu channel list during interrupt routines. When a channel was being deleted, there was a possibility that an interrupt could be generated, leading to the access of a freed channel structure. This situation could result in undefined behavior or crashes, as the interrupt handler might attempt to access memory that had already been deallocated. The patch addresses this by implementing RCU (Read-Copy-Update) protection, ensuring that the channel is not freed until it is safe to do so, thus preventing the use-after-free problem.
